recognize_zh: 視野中央一顆偏藍紫色的多染性紅血球 (polychromatophilic RBC) 內，可見細線狀、扭成迴圈或 8 字形的紫紅色細環，這就是 Cabot 環；本圖未見說明中提到的箭頭，也無法清楚確認 Howell-Jolly 小體。
features: Polychromatophilic (bluish) red cell containing a thin, reddish-purple threadlike loop/figure-of-eight inclusion (Cabot ring)
Adjacent second polychromatophilic red cell without a definite inclusion
Background red cells with anisocytosis and occasional teardrop/tailed and spherocytic-appearing forms
Small dot-like density in one red cell is equivocal for a Howell-Jolly body at this resolution
No arrows are present in this image
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mild anisopoikilocytosis with scattered polychromatophilic red cells and occasional tailed forms. One polychromatophilic red cell contains a delicate, threadlike, reddish-purple looped inclusion in a figure-of-eight configuration, characteristic of a Cabot ring. The arrows mentioned in the caption are not present on this image, and a Howell-Jolly body cannot be confidently identified. Findings are consistent with a Cabot ring in the setting of accelerated erythropoiesis, as seen in hemolytic or megaloblastic anemia.

ddx.vs: Malaria rings have a distinct blue cytoplasmic ring with one or two dense red chromatin dots, not a thin continuous figure-of-eight thread.
Babesia forms are small pleomorphic rings or tetrads (Maltese cross) with chromatin dots and no loop figure.
Basophilic stippling consists of multiple fine or coarse blue dots dispersed throughout the cell rather than a continuous thread.
Pappenheimer bodies are small peripheral clustered dots that stain with Prussian blue, not ring-shaped threads.
